reference_record.basis_note: The DOI/title/year are a prior source-manifest record used as the comparison target; this C1 experiment does not independently authenticate that record or paper.

claim_ceiling: One live Crossref interface comparison for one public citation only. Provider rows and hashes do not establish citation correctness generally, source authenticity, article content, scientific support, recall, reliability, latency distribution, or cost.
comparison_method: Same exact public citation text, same Crossref v1 Works endpoint, and rows=2; compare the dedicated query.bibliographic adapter with the existing general query adapter. The literal query is not copied into this evidence file.

candidates.title: Causal inference in the medical domain: a survey
Causal Inference with Complex Survey Designs

records.title: Causal Inference with Complex Survey Designs

request_accounting: One specialized request plus two identical generic requests. The first generic run summary omitted record rows in the local display; a second same-input retrieval produced the same request and response SHA-256 values and captured the bounded rows. Both generic response hashes are identical.
same_task_findings: The dedicated query.bibliographic response returned the previously recorded DOI 10.1007/s10489-024-05338-9 at provider rank 1 with exact title/year match to the earlier manifest record.
The general query response returned two other works and did not include the previously recorded DOI in its top two rows.
The outcome is specific to one citation and two returned rows; it is not a sensitivity, precision, recall, accuracy, or broad provider-quality estimate.
The specialized adapter reports up to two candidates and no DOI verdict. The general query tool remains useful for broader topic discovery and up to ten rows, so the tools coexist by task scope.
retirement_decision: Retire no existing tool; preserve the generic Crossref search for topic discovery. Keep the new citation matcher optional and default-off.
cost_comparison: UNKNOWN; the request count is observed, but comparative latency distribution, human review time, availability, bandwidth cost, and billed cost were not measured.
